title: One Ångström Inside the Cori Cycle & the Acid Organelle — Gerty & Carl Cori's Glycogen Phosphorylase & G6Pase, Christian de Duve's Centrifuged Lysosome & George Palade's Secretory Pathway (PDB 1FA9, 9JTM, 6WM2, 1LYB)

teenKit.tldr: Your body has a genius recycling loop that turns burning sprint lactate back into fuel, alongside microscopic acid bags that eat cellular trash without melting your organs.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Understanding these metabolic gears reveals how our cells fight off disease, handle high-intensity energy, and stay alive without accidentally digesting themselves from the inside out.
keyTakeaways: The Cori Cycle acts as a full-body recycling system, taking toxic lactic acid from hard-working muscles and converting it back into usable glucose in the liver.
Christian de Duve discovered lysosomes by accident after leaving test tubes in a cold fridge over a long weekend, revealing microscopic sacks of acid that dissolve cellular waste.
At the atomic scale of one Ångström, specialized molecular machinery like the V-ATPase pump and glycogen phosphorylase keep these survival loops spinning with exact thermodynamic precision.

vocab.meaning: The metabolic highway where muscles send sprint lactate to the liver to be remade into fresh energy glucose.
A membrane-enclosed cellular stomach packed with harsh, flesh-melting acids and enzymes to chop up cellular trash.
The cellular scissors enzyme that snips stored sugar molecules off glycogen chains to release instant energy.
A microscopic motor pump that burns fuel to cram protons inside organelles, keeping their internal acid levels lethal to debris.

quiz.question: What is the primary job of the Cori Cycle during an intense sprint?
options: To pump oxygen directly into leg muscle fibers
To scoop up toxic lactic acid and recycle it back into fuel
To melt away damaged cellular proteins using high-powered acid
To freeze the body's core temperature during a physical workout
quiz.explanation: The Cori Cycle rescues the body from metabolic gridlock by converting hard-earned sprint lactate back into liver glucose.

quiz.question: How was the lysosome initially discovered by Christian de Duve?
options: By building the world's first X-ray crystal microscope
By leaving rat-liver cell fractions sitting in a cold refrigerator over a long weekend
By observing a sprinter's heart rate drop during a marathon
By synthesizing artificial stomach acid in a test tube
quiz.explanation: A fortunate weekend in the icebox allowed enzymes to leak out of the fragile membranes, tipping off researchers to the existence of lysosomes.

quiz.question: Why don't lysosomes normally dissolve the entire cell they live inside?
options: Because they are protected by tough, tightly controlled surrounding membranes
Because cellular trash neutralizes all of their acid instantly
Because they only contain water and harmless sugars
Because cells have no internal membranes
quiz.explanation: Lysosomes keep their lethal digestive enzymes safely locked inside protective membranes so they only digest targeted waste.
